record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.context_brief: relations among weak embeddings of L1
record.original_question: Suppose L1[0,1] sign-embeds into a Banach space X. Must L1[0,1] then Gδ-embed into X? Suppose instead that L1[0,1] Gδ-embeds into X. Must L1[0,1] semi-embed into X? More generally, does sign-embedding of L1[0,1] into X already imply semi-embedding of L1[0,1] into X?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. A) Suppose that L1 sign-embeds into X . Does L1 Gδ -embed into X ? B) Suppose that L1 Gδ -embeds into X . Does L1 semi-embed into X ? C) Suppose that L1 sign-embeds into X . Does L1 semi-embed into X ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$ denote the space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$ with its usual norm. Recall the following notions of weak embedding of $L_1$ into $X$.

(i) A bounded linear operator $T : L_1 \to X$ is called a semi-embedding if $T$ is one-to-one and $T$ maps the closed unit ball $B_{L_1}$ to a closed subset of $X$.

(ii) A bounded linear operator $T : L_1 \to X$ is called a $G_\delta$-embedding if $T$ is one-to-one and $T(B_{L_1})$ is a $G_\delta$ subset of $X$ (i.e. a countable intersection of open sets).

(iii) A bounded linear operator $T : L_1 \to X$ is called a sign-embedding if $T$ is one-to-one and there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $\|T f\| \ge \delta$ for every $f \in L_1$ with $|f| = \mathbf 1_{[0,1]}$ a.e. (equivalently, for every $\{-1,+1\}$-valued $f$).

One says that $L_1$ sign-embeds (respectively $G_\delta$-embeds, semi-embeds) into $X$ if there exists such an operator $T : L_1 \to X$. It is known that
$$\text{semi-embedding} \Longrightarrow G_\delta\text{-embedding} \Longrightarrow \text{sign-embedding}.$$

Determine whether the following implications hold for an arbitrary Banach space $X$:

(A) If $L_1$ sign-embeds into $X$, does $L_1$ necessarily $G_\delta$-embed into $X$?

(B) If $L_1$ $G_\delta$-embeds into $X$, does $L_1$ necessarily semi-embed into $X$?

(C) If $L_1$ sign-embeds into $X$, does $L_1$ necessarily semi-embed into $X$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search returned background literature on semi-embeddings and Gδ-embeddings of L1 (e.g., Bourgain–Rosenthal-style results showing that if L1 semi-embeds into Y then Y contains ℓ1), but no source verifying that the three implications among sign-, Gδ-, and semi-embeddability of L1[0,1] have been resolved. The current status of these implications could not be confirmed from available sources.

status_evidence.snippet: A semi-embedding is a one-to-one operator mapping the closed unit ball onto a closed set; if L1 semi-embeds into Y then Y contains ℓ1.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on semi-embeddings of L1 but does not resolve the listed implications.
